memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not oppress a foreigner; you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners, because you were foreigners in Egypt." - Exodus 23:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again God appeals not just to a rule but to memory and empathy. Do not oppress the foreigner, He says, because you know exactly how it feels — you were foreigners in Egypt. Israel had tasted the bitterness of being outsiders, vulnerable and mistreated. God will not let them forget that feeling, because remembering it is meant to make them tender toward others in the same position.

There is deep wisdom in this. God often uses our own past hurts to grow compassion in us. The person who has been lonely can spot loneliness in others. The one who has been excluded knows how much a welcome means. Our scars, rather than making us hard, can make us the most gentle and understanding people of all — if we let God shape them that way.

This is a call to a compassionate imagination: to pause and remember how it feels to be on the other side. Before we judge or overlook the outsider, God invites us to remember our own moments of feeling small, unwelcome, or afraid. And ultimately, we who follow Christ were all once spiritual foreigners, far from God, yet He drew us near with kindness (Eph 2:12-13). Having been welcomed by such grace, let us become a welcoming people, tender toward every outsider we meet.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
How can I let my own past hurts grow compassion rather than hardness?
Who is the "foreigner" or outsider I might be overlooking right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You welcomed me when I was far from You. Help me remember how it feels to be an outsider, and make me tender and welcoming toward those who feel that way now. Amen.
